editorial.description_en: Iron-rich soil: the first entry here that anyone would call red rather than brown.
editorial.description_ja: 鉄分の多い土のような、赤みのある色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.716, C 0.080, h 48.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 赤 (aka, red) + 土 (tsuchi, earth). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Red Earth" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 赤土. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — su-yaki at ΔE00 3.9, tsuchi-gawara at ΔE00 9.0, kari-ato at ΔE00 10.9. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (228°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
